_meta.notes: C01 client foundation: quality tiers, resolution floor, camera smoothing, idle-drop timeout. C02/C03 own the plant and environment shader values.

target_fps.notes: Render-loop target frames per second on the current tier.

fps_warning_threshold.notes: Fraction of target_fps at which the client downgrades resolution.

resolution_floor.notes: Minimum renderer pixel ratio relative to devicePixelRatio. Was 0.5: on a machine that cannot reach target_fps the band sat on the floor for the whole session, so the picture - and every name tag in the 3D scene - was drawn at half resolution and upscaled.

max_pixel_ratio.notes: Maximum renderer pixel ratio. The band never recovers past the display's own density, so this is the absolute bound: on a 150% display it stops at 1.5 and on a 2x display it may use 2.

camera_smoothing.notes: OrbitControls dampingFactor. Damping is per frame, so 0.05 (Three's default) is a ~0.3 s glide at 60 fps and a ~0.7 s glide at 27 fps: dragging the camera read as input lag rather than weight.

camera_mode.notes: The camera rig. free: a flying eye - W/A/S/D follow the whole view vector, the eye neither follows the terrain nor is clamped out of it, and Root Sight's cavity clamps are off (the near-side cut that keeps the pit readable from inside it lands with the volume terrain). ground: the old ground-following rig, where the rig rises with the terrain and the eye is kept out of the dirt.

camera_min_distance_root.notes: Minimum orbit distance while inspecting the root layer (Root Sight on, or the camera/target below the surface), so root tips stay readable without letting the camera enter the seed above ground.

camera_max_polar_angle.notes: Max polar angle in radians (~177 degrees, allows looking straight down).

camera_start_distance.notes: Initial and recenter orbit distance from the player plant. Close enough to read a seedling.

camera_pan_speed.notes: WASD/arrow camera pan speed in world units per second.

camera_zoom_speed.notes: Dolly speed for the - and + keys in metres per second: the camera travels towards or away from its orbit target, the field of view never changes.

camera_collision_enabled.notes: Pull the camera in when the line of sight from its target would pass through a solid physics collider (terrain).

camera_collision_margin.notes: Gap kept between the camera and whatever solid object it is pushed away from.

idle_drop_timeout_ms.notes: Ms of no input before the render loop throttles to 10 fps.

shadow_bias.notes: Depth offset for the sun's shadow map. Without it the soil plane shadows itself at low sun angles and the near ground goes grey.

shadow_normal_bias.notes: Normal-aligned shadow offset in metres; the soil plane needs it because a shadow texel covers a large patch of ground.

planet_radius_m.notes: Radius of the planet the world is the surface of. The play area is a cap at its pole; 0 keeps a flat plane.

planet_view_distance_multiplier.notes: Orbit-view camera distance from the planet centre, as a multiple of planet_radius_m.

planet_view_far_multiplier.notes: Orbit-view far plane, as a multiple of planet_radius_m.

planet_view_min_distance_multiplier.notes: Orbit-view minimum distance from the planet centre, as a multiple of planet_radius_m; keeps the camera outside the body.

planet_view_near_multiplier.notes: Orbit-view near plane, as a multiple of planet_radius_m. Keeps depth precision usable at planetary distances.

debug_overlay_enabled.notes: Toggle the C01 debug overlay (fps, triangles, draw calls, memory, network). Its key lives in controls.json as the debug_toggle action.

pause_on_hidden.notes: Pause the render loop and stop sending INPUT when the tab is hidden.

sky_zenith_day.notes: Sky zenith color during clear day.

sky_horizon_day.notes: Sky horizon color during clear day.

sky_zenith_dusk.notes: Sky zenith color during dawn/dusk transitions.

sky_horizon_dusk.notes: Sky horizon color during dawn/dusk transitions.

sky_night_min_light.notes: Floor on the weather light that scales the night sky palette: a stormy night is darker than a clear one, but never so dark the palette disappears.

skylight_desaturation.notes: How far the fill light's sky colour is pulled to neutral. At 0 every upward-facing surface (the inside of the Root Sight pit included) is tinted the sky's full blue; at 1 the skylight is grey.

sky_zenith_telegraph.notes: Sky zenith color during storm telegraph phase.

sky_horizon_telegraph.notes: Sky horizon color during storm telegraph phase.

sun_color_day.notes: Directional sun color during clear day.

sun_color_night.notes: Directional celestial light color during night (moonlight).

sun_intensity_day.notes: Direct solar light intensity at peak noon.

sun_intensity_night.notes: Direct celestial light intensity at midnight. Lifted from 0.15 so night is dark, not blind: the ground keeps its texture and a plant reads as a silhouette. At 0.6 it is twice the night ambient, so the moon is the brightest light there is: a surface facing it is moonlit, one facing away falls back on the ambient instead of both sitting at the same value.

ambient_intensity_night.notes: Ambient light intensity during night. Lifted from 0.15 with the moonlight: below that, night on the young-plant framing was indistinguishable from a black screen.

ambient_fade_tau_s.notes: Time constant in seconds for the ambient day/night fade. The frame step is exp(-dt/tau), so dusk takes the same wall-clock time at 30, 60 or 144 fps; the old fixed 0.3-per-frame step ran three times faster at 144 fps.

fog_near_clear.notes: Fog near distance during clear weather.

fog_far_clear.notes: Fog far distance during clear weather.

fog_near_storm.notes: Fog near distance during active storm.

fog_far_storm.notes: Fog far distance during active storm.

rain_particle_count.notes: Number of precipitation particles simulated in camera volume.

rain_particle_speed.notes: Vertical descent speed of rain particles in m/s.

rain_box_width.notes: Horizontal dimensions of rain bounding volume centered on camera.

rain_box_height.notes: Vertical dimension of rain bounding volume.

rain_streak_length.notes: Length of rain streaks in world units.

rain_streak_width.notes: Width of rain streaks in world units.

rain_max_velocity.notes: Maximum rain particle velocity for streak scaling.

lightning_flash_duration_ms.notes: Duration of an atmospheric lightning flash in milliseconds.

lightning_intensity_boost.notes: Peak light intensity multiplier during lightning flash.

rain_slant.notes: Horizontal drift of rain streaks per unit fallen; the fall angle.

sun_orbital_distance.notes: Orbit radius that places the directional light on the visual sun.

weather_transition_ms.notes: Cross-fade between weather sky/fog presets; short values snap, long values smear.

lightning_max_intensity.notes: Peak flash intensity the storm weather state emits.

soil_dry_color.notes: Terrain soil tint when moisture is low. Warm brown so dry dirt does not read as grey.

soil_wet_color.notes: Terrain soil tint when moisture is high or after rain.

soil_mineral_tint.notes: Subtle mineral accent tone on ground terrain.

soil_grain_strength.notes: Per-pixel mineral hash on the ground. The old 0.08 speckled the dirt; the Root Sight dome colour is the smoother target.

soil_mineral_strength.notes: How much the per-tile mineral channel tints the ground.

terrain_mesh_subdivisions.notes: Subdivision segments of the detailed inner terrain patch. At 180 m width, 256 gives ~0.70 m cells, enough to resolve the terrain field instead of flattening its divots and burying the seed.

terrain_radius.notes: World radius of the ground terrain mesh.

terrain_amplitude_m.notes: Peak procedural relief above the base surface, in metres. The shared terrain field reads the same value server-side.

soil_depth_m.notes: Depth of the topsoil layer below the surface; below it is subsoil, then bedrock.

camera_pivot_height_m.notes: Height of the orbit pivot above the player's feet. A pivot on the ground cannot look up: every angle that points above the horizon puts the eye underground, so the ground clamp pulls it back. Orbiting at head height lets the eye stand on the terrain and look at the sky.

node_pick_tie_m.notes: Two pick spheres the ray meets within this distance are the same point on screen, so the deeper node wins. A parent's sphere contains its child; without the tie rule a click on the child selected the parent.

drop_pick_distance_m.notes: How far the pointer may reach to pick up a world drop. Drops are small markers; without a reach limit a click on the horizon would collect one across the field.

camera_ground_touch_m.notes: How close the eye may get to the ground when Root Sight is closed. It may touch the dirt and look along it, never pass through: this is a contact epsilon, not a stand-off.

player_gravity_mps2.notes: Downward acceleration of the observer rig onto the terrain.

player_spawn_height_m.notes: Height the observer rig is dropped from when it spawns.

root_aura_radius.notes: 3D proximity aura radius around root nodes for subterranean sight cutaway.

webgpu_enabled.notes: Enable the WebGPU plant overlay. Off by default because it draws to a second canvas with its own depth buffer, so plants cannot be occluded by terrain or dirt; the WebGL renderer shares the scene depth and sorts correctly.

webgpu_max_plants.notes: Maximum plants supported by WebGPU compute-driven renderer.

webgpu_tier0_threshold.notes: Projected pixel size threshold for Tier 0 (full mesh).

webgpu_tier1_threshold.notes: Projected pixel size threshold for Tier 1 (mid mesh).

webgpu_tier2_threshold.notes: Projected pixel size threshold for Tier 2 (multi-view impostor).

webgpu_tier3_threshold.notes: Projected pixel size threshold for Tier 3 (single-view billboard).

webgpu_min_dwell_time.notes: Minimum dwell time in seconds before tier change.

webgpu_impostor_enabled.notes: Bake impostor atlases for far plants instead of drawing their geometry every frame.

webgpu_impostor_update_interval_ms.notes: Minimum gap between impostor re-bakes of the same plant, in milliseconds.

webgpu_vram_budget_bytes.notes: Total vertex and index bytes the WebGPU buffer pool may hold before it evicts.

webgpu_vram_max_vertex_bytes.notes: Per-buffer vertex ceiling; a plant whose vertex buffer would exceed it is not uploaded.

webgpu_vram_max_index_bytes.notes: Per-buffer index ceiling, same rule as the vertex ceiling.

webgpu_texture_array_size.notes: Edge length of each plant-variation texture array layer, in texels.

webgpu_texture_array_layers.notes: Variation layers in the plant texture array; getVariationIndex must stay below this.

node_pick_radius.notes: Minimum world-space pick radius for node selection during growth.

underground_view_color.notes: Backdrop and fog colour while the camera is below the surface with Root Sight open.

growth_aim_ring_scale.notes: Aim ring radius as a multiple of the emerging segment's own thickness, capped at the node's radius.

growth_aim_ring_min.notes: Minimum aim ring radius in metres, so thin roots still show a usable ring.

growth_aim_ring_thickness.notes: Tube thickness of the aim ring in metres; kept in world units so small rings stay visible.

growth_aim_grab_px.notes: Screen radius around the part where a drag turns the aim arrow; elsewhere a drag orbits the camera.

growth_aim_reach_min.notes: Minimum aim arrow length in metres.

growth_aim_tube_radius.notes: Radius of the curved aim arrow shaft in metres.

growth_aim_head_radius.notes: Radius of the aim arrow head cone in metres.

growth_aim_head_length.notes: Length of the aim arrow head cone in metres.

growth_aim_tip_radius.notes: Radius of the bud dot at the aim arrow point, in metres.

growth_aim_curve_bend.notes: Sideways bend of the aim arrow, as a fraction of its length. 0 keeps the preview straight like the real segment.

growth_aim_curve_wobble.notes: Secondary wave of the aim arrow, as a fraction of its length. 0 keeps the preview straight like the real segment.

soil_crack_strength.notes: AL-04 dirt: how strongly dried fissures darken the soil. Off by default: ridged noise draws dark lines over the ground, which read as scratches across the palette's flat dirt rather than as dry soil. Turn up only when a cracked crust is wanted.

soil_pebble_strength.notes: AL-04 dirt: small rounded stones mixed into the topsoil, in colour and in the bump normal, so the ground catches light like loose dirt. Off by default: the speckle breaks up the palette's flat dirt, which is the look the soil ramp is for.

atmosphere_extinction_r.notes: AL-04: red extinction per metre at sea level. Art-directed for a hazy day, not Earth air.

atmosphere_extinction_g.notes: AL-04: green extinction per metre at sea level.

atmosphere_extinction_b.notes: AL-04: blue extinction per metre at sea level. Higher than red so distance cools.

atmosphere_scale_height_m.notes: AL-04: height over which air density falls by 1/e, in metres.

atmosphere_sun_phase_g.notes: AL-04: Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy. Forward scattering picks out the sun and backlights silhouettes.

atmosphere_in_scatter.notes: AL-04: strength of sun in-scatter mixed into fogged surfaces and the sky.

atmosphere_horizon_boost.notes: AL-04: extra density at grazing view angles, so the horizon reads heavier than the zenith.

gpu_band_min_ms.notes: AL-03: frame cost below this restores detail. 10 ms at 60 Hz leaves rendering headroom.

gpu_band_max_ms.notes: AL-03: frame cost above this spends detail, resolution first, then draw distance, then tier.

quality_hold_ms.notes: AL-03: minimum time between quality decisions, so the controller cannot oscillate.

quality_warmup_ms.notes: AL-03: cost is ignored for this long after the first sample, so shader compiles and uploads during load do not spend detail.

quality_smoothing.notes: AL-03: EMA weight for a new frame-cost sample. Lower is steadier, so one hitch cannot move a lever.

draw_distance_floor.notes: AL-03: lowest draw-distance scale. Detail is only removed down to this before the tier is lowered.

size_classes.notes: ADR-027: organism size class is presentation. A giant is framed from further away and may hold more detailed plants, because LOD assigns tiers by projected pixel size.

fog_horizon_mist_scale.notes: Fog distance multiplier when the sun is on the horizon: low sun thickens the air, so dawn and dusk carry mist instead of looking like a neutral bright hour.

exposure_day.notes: Renderer exposure with the sun high. Applied through the renderer's LinearToneMapping, which is enabled for exactly this reason: with no tone mapping three ignores exposure, so the grade would be a knob with no effect. At 1.0 the output is unchanged.

exposure_horizon.notes: Renderer exposure when the sun is on the horizon: a slight lift for golden hour.

exposure_night.notes: Renderer exposure at night. 0.92 crushed the night so hard that the young-plant framing - 3 m away, 30 degrees down - was a frame of unlit soil and read as a black screen; the cup is now only a tint, not a blackout.

camera_young_max_distance.notes: A fitted plant closer than this (a seed or a sprout) is framed from the young-plant elevation: at 1.5 m a 15-degree eye sits 0.4 m up and the soil fills the frame.

camera_young_elevation.notes: Vertical part of the framing direction for a young plant, before normalisation (mature plants use the shallow side view). 0.55 is roughly 30 degrees above the target.

camera_recenter_elevation.notes: Vertical part of the direction Space (and a double-click on empty ground) returns the camera to, before normalisation, while keeping the player's azimuth. 0.27 is roughly 15 degrees above the target. It resets a pitch the player panned to; it never spins the view.
